summary: Intermittent zero-trust agent disconnect after AP handoff causing VPN session auth failure and internal DNS resolution loss
description: Multiple employees in the SF office report that when they move between adjacent access points (short walk between desks) their Zero-Trust agent (corporate secure-agent) briefly disconnects, followed by the system being unable to reauthenticate the VPN session for internal services. Symptoms include failure to resolve internal hostnames (corp.local), intermittent 401/403 errors when hitting internal APIs, and resumed access only after manual agent restart or 30-90s. This ticket tracks investigation with Networking, SRE, and Endpoint teams.
impact: Several engineers experienced interrupted access to internal build services, K8s dashboards, and repo mirrors during office mobility. Productivity impact reported across 6 unique users during the morning sprint. No customer-facing services were affected.
steps_to_reproduce: Connect a MacBook or Windows laptop to corp-ssid on AP-A (near desk cluster A).
Authenticate and confirm secure-agent shows 'Connected' and can reach internal service https://k8s-console.corp.local.
Walk ~10-15 meters to AP-B coverage (adjacent office cluster) to trigger 802.11 handoff/roaming.
Attempt to curl internal hostname; observe DNS resolution failures or 401 from internal proxy.
logs: Secure-agent log snippet (03-12T09:21:14Z): INFO handoff detected: old_ap=ap-24 new_ap=ap-27, initiating reauth sequence
Secure-agent (03-12T09:21:15Z): WARN tls session dropped: timeout waiting for server-challenge
VPN-gateway syslog (03-12T09:21:16Z): NOTICE auth failed for device-id=abc123: token-expired/invalidation
DHCP controller (03-12T09:21:15Z): INFO DHCP rebind requested leaseid=42 for mac=aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff
Windows EventID 455: Network profile changed during authentication
tcpdump on edge (03-12T09:21:16Z): observed SYN to auth.corp.internal, no response from auth service for 10s while mobile client rebinds IP
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: AP handoff causes a short L2 disconnect and NIC metric flip on endpoints; secure-agent treats this as network change and tears down session before completing token refresh.

Reproduced consistently on one MacBook Pro running secure-agent v3.2.1 and on a Windows laptop running secure-agent v3.1.9, but not reproducible on some Linux laptops (likely platform behavior differences).

Wireless controller shows <200ms of probe/association chatter during handoff; not grossly high. However AP-B sends a DHCP rebind hint which causes client to request new lease concurrently with secure-agent reauth.

Observed race between agent's token refresh (using cached refresh token) and DHCP lease rebind which temporarily changes source IP; auth backend rejects refresh due to seen source IP change in our session policy. This triggers immediate session invalidation instead of transparent refresh.
Auth policy currently includes strict source-ip binding for refresh tokens in prod for office networks (hardening introduced 2025-11), which may be too strict for short roaming events.
comments: Maya Chen (03-12): Filed after two devs reported interrupted CI uploads mid-sprint. Attached secure-agent log and time window.
Ethan Rivera (03-12): Assigned to investigate. Will reproduce with RRM telemetry and run a tcpdump from AP-B to edge during handoff.
Network Eng (03-13): Confirmed AP handoff sequence is normal; however some clients are aggressively renewing DHCP when receiving disassociation/association events.
SRE (03-13): Auth team suggests we can relax the source-ip binding for refresh token validation for 'office-wifi' ACL for short durations while we roll client fix.
Endpoint (03-14): Identified that secure-agent v3.2.2 (internal beta) includes a queued-refresh path that tolerates ephemeral NIC changes; testing underway.
Ethan Rivera (03-14): Added temporary mitigation to auth-proxy to accept refresh when last-seen-ip differs by office subnet mask and session age < 60s. Pushed config to staging for smoke tests.
root_cause: Race between endpoint DHCP rebind/network-change during AP handoff and refresh-token validation which enforces strict source-IP binding. The authentication policy invalidates the refresh when source IP changes, causing forced reauthentication failures and manual agent restarts for affected clients.
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation: Relax source-IP binding for refresh-token checks for 'office' network classification with a 60s grace window. Deployed to edge auth-proxy (canary in us-west-office-sf).

Medium-term: Roll secure-agent client update (v3.2.2) which implements queued refresh and performs graceful retry on transient NIC changes. Endpoint team PR: github.com/redwood/secure-agent/pull/512 (internal).

Long-term: Update auth policy doc and add telemetry to measure refresh rejects caused by ip-change and correlate with wireless handoffs. Create a cookbook for tuning DHCP lease timers and client rebind behaviors on APs.
Follow-ups: Create INT ticket to roll policy change to other offices after 72h canary. Notify Workspace Ops to evaluate AP steering/roaming tuning to reduce aggressive DHCP behavior.
